summary: Created a 10-phase (~12h) implementation plan. Core design decision: never rename a live FTS id; instead bridge the index.json .id namespace and .literature.db chunks_data.doc_id namespace through the sources/<dir>/ component of each entry's .path -- a derivation literature-search.sh already performs at four sites. Planning-time re-measurement confirmed the research counts (399 entries, 0 null-id, 189 parents, 204 FTS doc_ids, 32 FTS-only, 17 index-only) and refined the reconciliation residue from '49 disagreements' to 15 FTS-only directories lacking a parent entry, 2 duplicate chunk directories, and 1 index entry whose conversion was rejected. Path derivation covers 202/204 FTS doc_ids vs 172/204 for .id, so 31 of the 49 divergences are closed by code alone. All three open decisions settled explicitly with rationale: (A) new ingests move under sources/<id>/ -- build-index is placement-agnostic (recursive find for chunks.json), so there is no FTS migration risk, and it switches on fidelity-audit targeting for free; (B) chunk granularity 1:1 with chunks.json/FTS rows so briefing counts and --toc counts agree by construction, legacy part-granularity books explicitly not retrofitted; (C) reconcile by path bridge plus parent entries under bare ids for the 15 uncovered directories, with explicit NO ACTION on the 14 paired curated-id entries. Every id-touching phase (2,3,4,5,8) requires verification BY EXECUTION -- running --toc and a project-filtered search, with reading the script named as unacceptable evidence. All code edits target agent-system/extensions/literature/**; Phase 8 is flagged as a manual/scripted data change in the separate ~/Projects/Literature/ repo, committed there, touching no file in this repository.
